findings.element: Tasks `.tick` inside `.lrow` (List view at every width, and the only view a phone gets) and inside `.tpTitleRow` (the task sheet)
findings.problem: A completed task's checkbox is drawn identically to an uncompleted one. Diffing 33 computed properties across the element and both pseudo-elements — background, box-shadow, border, colour, opacity, the SVG's colour/stroke and the check path's stroke — a `.lrow[data-done]` and a `.lrow` without it differ in ZERO properties at 390, at 768, and at 1440 with List chosen from the switch. On the board at 1920 the same pair differs in 11. Driven on a 390 phone: tapping the tick on "Confirm marquee sides with the hire company" leaves background rgba(0,0,0,0), box-shadow inset 0 0 0 1.4px rgba(17,17,17,.28) and colour rgba(0,0,0,0) exactly as they were, while aria-checked flips false→true and the name flips "Mark done"→"Mark not done". The control she pressed does not change one pixel; the confirmation is a lane word 300px to the right. On the task sheet the same empty circle sits beside a struck-through title under a green DONE eyebrow. Cause: every done rule is scoped to the BOARD card — `.card[data-done] .tick` (2326), `.card[data-just-done] .tick` + its `checkDraw` (2535-6), `.card[data-done] .tick:hover/:focus-visible` (3160-1), and the forced-colors pair (3193-4) — and `listRow()` (12686) emits `<article class="lrow" data-done>`, not `.card`. The forced-colors half inverts it: because `.card:not([data-done]) .tick svg {display:none}` never matches a list row, under forcedColors:active all 13 list ticks paint their check, 8 of them not done (verified; the board correctly gives none/block). This is the most-pressed control in the product, in the phone's only view, and it is the one place on the surface where the pixels and the accessible name say opposite things.
findings.fix: In _gate-suite.html widen the five done-state selector groups from the board card to both row types: line 2326 `.card[data-done] .tick` → `:is(.card, .lrow)[data-done] .tick`; lines 2535-2536 `.card[data-just-done] .tick` and `.card[data-just-done] .tick svg path` → `:is(.card, .lrow)[data-just-done]` (and add the `data-just-done` attribute in `listRow()` on completion exactly as the card branch sets it); line 2546-2547 the reduced-motion group the same way; lines 3160-3161 `.card[data-done] .tick:hover, .card[data-done] .tick:focus-visible` → `:is(.card, .lrow)[data-done] .tick:...`; lines 3193-3194 `.card:not([data-done]) .tick svg` → `:is(.card, .lrow):not([data-done]) .tick svg` and `.card[data-done] .tick` → `:is(.card, .lrow)[data-done] .tick`. Then make the task sheet's tick take the same rules by giving `.tpTitleRow`'s wrapper `data-done` when the task is done and adding it to the same `:is()` list. No new colour, weight or token — the treatment already exists and is already ratified on the board. Finally, make the three surfaces agree on the rest of "done": today the board greys nothing and does not strike, the list row greys the title to rgba(17,17,17,.62) at weight 600 and does not strike, and the sheet strikes it. Pick one (the board's fill plus the sheet's strike) and use it in all three.

findings.element: Timeline `.b-edit`, across layout, opened by `[data-act="add"]` ("Add a moment") or by a moment's `.b-grab`
findings.problem: Opening a moment's editor on the across desk leaves it below the fold and scrolls nothing. Measured at five desk viewports, both paths: 1280x900 grab top 998 / add top 1068, 1440x900 grab 902 / add 972, 1440x960 grab 972 / add 972 — 0% of the panel visible in all six; 1600x1000 and 1920x1000 show 28px of its top edge, 5%. The first control is off screen in every case. `.app.sheet` is the real scroller (scrollHeight 1680, clientHeight 924) and its scrollTop is 0 before and after, every time. Nothing is announced either — the live region is empty. So at 1440x960 the whole visible result of pressing the product's one filled primary action is a "New moment / Fri 17 Jul / 1" placeholder near the origin plus every other label swapping sides of the rail; the name field, four date steppers, Shown/Hidden, Close and Delete are 12-48px past the bottom edge with no cue they exist. `keepInBand` (21926) is behaving correctly to its own stated law — it keeps the ITEM in band and consults the panel only when the panel is position:fixed — and the open-time focus call uses `.focus({preventScroll:true})`, which also suppresses the browser's own scroll-on-focus. Pressing Tab afterwards does bring it in (native focus scroll puts the first control at top 460), which is why the keyboard path feels fine and the pointer path is blind. The behaviour gate stands next to this and misses it: `across @w · placing a moment is not done blind` asserts that at least one of the eight `.b-grab` handles stays on screen (7-8 do) and never asks whether the editor is.
findings.fix: At the point where the across-layout editor is opened (the `.b-edit` open branch, not the stepper handlers), after the panel renders, scroll the `.app.sheet` ancestor so the panel's head and its date row sit inside the band — reuse the ancestor walk keepInBand already performs (`for (var up = root; up && up !== document.body; up = up.parentElement)` picking the first overflowY auto/scroll element whose scrollHeight exceeds clientHeight) and set `box.scrollTop += Math.round(panelRect.top - boxRect.top - 24)` when `panelRect.top + 240 > box.clientHeight`. Leave keepInBand itself untouched so the stepper contract ("moves the item on the measure and moves nothing else") still holds. Simplest equivalent: drop `preventScroll: true` from that one open-time focus call only.

findings.element: Notes review, the repaint that renders the "Everything is decided." sheet
findings.problem: Emptying the review queue drops the keyboard out of the document on the last step. Driven twice at 1440x960, once with the K accelerator and once with real clicks on "Just keep it": after decisions 1 through 7 focus lands on `P.handBody`, the next note's body — a deliberate, correct restoration. After decision 8, the one that completes the flow, `document.activeElement` is BODY. The next Tab lands on `.headNext` at the very top of the sheet, so the reading position restarts at the page head; a screen-reader user hears "Kept in Notes. 0 left. Nothing left to decide." from a focus position of nowhere. The completion sheet already renders exactly one first move — the filled "Back to your notes" button — and it is not focused (`document.activeElement === btn` is false). Every other repaint in this product restores focus correctly: the tick, the keyboard drop, the seam send, the crossing into Tasks, undo. This is the only one that does not, and it is the terminal beat of the flow Notes exists for.
findings.fix: In the review branch that renders the "Everything is decided." sheet, after paint call `sheet.querySelector('[data-act="back-to-notes"]').focus({ preventScroll: true })` (the same restoration shape the per-card branch already uses, which focuses `.handBody`). If that button carries no data-act, match it by class on the completion card's primary action.

findings.element: Notes `.headNext` — "Mara & Finn / Saturday 3 October, in 79 days" in the sheet head
findings.problem: The head's scope control is a real, working, well-built filter that nothing on screen identifies as pressable. It is `<button data-act="scope" aria-pressed="false" aria-label="...Press to see only these notes.">`; pressing it narrows the index from 14 rows to 3, flips the h1 from "All your notes" to "Your notes, narrowed", underlines itself and prints an "All 14 notes" way-out pill — good work. But at rest it carries no chevron, no rule, no fill and no underline, and its hover is a no-op: comparing every computed property of the button and both children between rest and :hover gives zero changed properties, and a rendered 700x60 crop of the head band is byte-identical between the two states (1300 bytes, Buffer.equals true). The cause is one line — `.headNext:hover b { color: var(--ink) }` at 4441 against `--ink-1: var(--ink)` at 4194, so the hover repaints #111111 as #111111. Its opposite number in Tasks, `.projSwitch`, does the same job in the same head slot and ships an SVG chevron. The consequence for a first-time reader is that the head parses as one sentence — "All your notes, Mara & Finn, Saturday 3 October, in 79 days" — which is a false description of what is on screen (14 notes across four notebooks), and the control that would make it true is invisible; the affordance only arrives after the state has already changed.
findings.fix: Give `.headNext` a rest-state affordance matched to `.projSwitch`: append the same chevron SVG that `.projSwitch` uses after the date span, at `--ink-3`, and add `[data-app="notes"] .headNext:hover { box-shadow: inset 0 -1px 0 var(--ink-4); }` so hover produces a visible change. Then either delete the dead `.headNext:hover b { color: var(--ink) }` at 4441 or repoint it at a colour that differs from `--ink-1`. When `aria-pressed="true"` the existing `inset 0 -2px 0 var(--indigo)` continues to win.

findings.element: Timeline `.b-copy` on the across measure, `[data-side="above"]` vs `[data-side="below"]`
findings.problem: The labels above and below the rail are not mirror images of each other; they read in two different orders. Measured at 1920 on timeline.owner-flight with the rail at y=682, distance of each label's optical centre from the rail, outward: above the rail it is day-count 35px, then date 51px, then title 73-85px; below the rail it is day-count 35px, then title 56px, then date 78px. The day-count is symmetric to the pixel and the title and date swap rings. It holds for all seven moments (16/37/51/79 above read number-date-title; 23/44/65 below read number-title-date). Cause, 8544-8556: `.b-copy` (DOM order title then date) is mirrored as a block by swapping `bottom:` for `top:` while its internal order is never reversed, so above the rail the last child ends up nearest and the first child farthest. Two consequences for scanning: the titles — the only thing on the measure that says what a moment IS — do not form a band, they alternate 73px above and 56px below and sit on opposite sides of their own dates; and the below-line order (number, title, date) is the order the down layout and the phone use, so the four above-line moments are the only place in the product that reads number-date-title.
findings.fix: Add `[data-app="timeline"] .b-measure[data-across="true"] .b-item[data-side="above"] .b-copy { display: flex; flex-direction: column-reverse; }` so that above the rail the visual order top-to-bottom becomes date then title, which read outward from the rail gives number, title, date — the same as below the rail, the down layout and the phone. The block's own position is unchanged, so `--away-h` and the placeAcross measurement stay valid.

biggestWin: Information integrity across three products that share one world. Every count on the surface derives from one accessor and none of them drift: the Notes index head says "8 to decide / 14 notes" and the five group tails sum to exactly 8 and 14; the Tasks head says "5 of 13 done / 38% / 5 with no day" and the lane counts, the dateless cards and the percentage all reconcile; the dense board's three "N more below" rows reconcile against 32; and when a note crosses the seam every one of those numbers moves together in one frame — Tasks goes 5 of 13 to 5 of 14, 38% to 36%, "5 with no day" to "6 with no day", To do 3 to 4, while Notes goes "8 to decide" to 7 and "3 so far" to 4. Turning on the overdue filter converts every lane count to shown/total (0/3, 1/3, 0/2, 0, 0/5), states itself in words, badges the Show control and offers the way back. The Timeline's measure is arithmetically honest to the pixel — today at x=209, the wedding at x=1876, 79 days, 21.1px per day, and every intermediate tick within 1.5px of daysFromToday x px-per-day, with the weekday names right for 2026 — and one clock governs all three products: "TODAY IS 16 JULY" on the Timeline, "Thursday 16 July, today" on a Notes group head, and 14 Jul as the single overdue chip in Tasks. That is the hardest property on the whole list and the one that decides whether a person can trust a surface, and it holds everywhere I pushed it.
